# unleash_api_token (Resource)

ApiToken schema

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "unleash_api_token" "frontend_token" {
  token_name  = "frontend_token"
  type        = "frontend"
  expires_at  = "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"
  projects    = ["*"]
  environment = "development"
}

resource "unleash_api_token" "frontend_token" {
  token_name  = "frontend_token"
  type        = "frontend"
  expires_at  = "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"
  projects    = ["default"]
  environment = "development"
}
```

## Rotate a token without interrupting consumers

Unleash token names are immutable. Changing `token_name` on an existing Terraform resource replaces the token and generates a new secret. Deleting the old token revokes its secret, so consumers still using it will lose access.

For a controlled rotation, use two separate applies with a consumer migration between them:

1. Keep the existing token resource unchanged and add a second resource with a different Terraform address and token name. Run `terraform plan` and verify that it only adds the new token, then run `terraform apply`.
2. Update consumers to use the new token secret and verify that they work before deleting the old token.
3. Remove the old token resource from the configuration. Run `terraform plan` and verify that it only deletes the old token, then run `terraform apply` to revoke it.

For example, if the existing resource is `unleash_api_token.edge_token`, keep that block and add `unleash_api_token.edge_token_next`:

```terraform
# Keep the existing resource and its configuration unchanged.
resource "unleash_api_token" "edge_token" {
  token_name  = "edge_token_prod"
  type        = "client"
  projects    = ["default"]
  environment = "production"
}

# Add this resource in the first apply.
resource "unleash_api_token" "edge_token_next" {
  token_name  = "edge_token_production"
  type        = "client"
  projects    = ["default"]
  environment = "production"
}
```

Use `unleash_api_token.edge_token_next.secret` when updating consumers. After the migration, remove only the `edge_token` block and retain `edge_token_next` at its existing Terraform address.

Terraform tracks each resource by its address in state; the provider locates the Unleash token using its secret or v2 identifier, rather than its name. Removing the old resource and adding the new resource in the same apply does not provide a migration window. Likewise, `create_before_destroy` can change replacement ordering, but does not pause for consumers to migrate between applies.

## Schema

### Optional

- `environment` (String) An environment the token has access to.
- `expires_at` (String) When the token expires
- `identifier` (String) Set if the token uses the new v2 format, used where v1 would use Secret
- `project` (String, Deprecated) A project the token belongs to.
- `projects` (Set of String) The list of projects this token has access to. If the token has access to specific projects they will be listed here. If the token has access to all projects it will be represented as `[*]`.
- `secure` (Boolean) If true the token uses the new v2 format and the full secret will never be returned after the creation call
- `token_name` (String) The name of the token. Changing this value replaces the token and creates a new secret. Deleting the old token revokes its secret; consumers must use the new secret.
- `type` (String) The type of the token.

### Read-Only

- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Secret token value.
